_about: Order 133 (117a item 4): the review tiers' rules as data, the one source. backend/app/review_tiers.py reads this file; scripts/gen_contract_types.py writes it into contracts/generated/review_tiers.ts, which the screen's crs/tiers.ts reads. contracts/fixtures/review_tier_cases.json holds the cases both sides must pass. Display only: no stored status or verdict is decided here.

word_edge._about: Order 135 (D1): a phrase is found only between word edges, and both engines mean the same thing by a word character: a Unicode letter (L*), a Unicode number (N*) or an underscore. Each phrase writes its edges as (?<!TOKEN) and (?!TOKEN); each engine puts its own spelling of that one class in place of the token. Python's str \w is exactly that class (test_133 checks every code point Python knows); JavaScript spells it [\p{L}\p{N}_] and needs the u flag. Known limit: a character first assigned after Unicode 15.0 (the database of Python 3.12) is no letter to the server and may be one to the screen. Never \b: JavaScript's \b knows only ASCII letters, so 'évalue conflict' read as 'value conflict' on the screen only.

fold._about: Order 135 (D2): the separators folded to one space, written out so both engines fold the same characters (Python's \s and JavaScript's \s differ: only JavaScript's has U+FEFF, only Python's has U+001C-U+001F and U+0085). The class is every character either engine calls white space, plus the invisible spaces U+200B (zero width space) and U+2060 (word joiner), plus underscore and hyphen. It holds every character Python's strip() and JavaScript's trim() remove, so after the fold both trim only spaces.
